context.title: Hezekiah Trusts the LORD
context.summary: Hezekiah removes the high places and smashes the bronze serpent. When Assyria's King Sennacherib invades, his spokesman stands outside Jerusalem's walls and mocks Judah's trust in the LORD.
context.background: Sennacherib's invasion of 701 BC is described in his own annals, which boast that he shut Hezekiah up in Jerusalem 'like a bird in a cage' but do not claim to have taken the city. Carved reliefs of his siege of Lachish (v. 14) decorated his palace in Nineveh.

customs.note: A title, not a name — a high Assyrian official. Tartan and Rabsaris are titles too.
Moses' bronze serpent (Numbers 21:8-9), which had become an object of worship.

watchFor: Judah's officials ask him to speak Aramaic, the diplomatic language, so the people on the wall won't understand (v. 26).
The key word 'trust' repeats throughout the speech (vv. 19–24, 30).

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Hezekiah
people.summary: Son of Ahaz (2 Kings 18:1; 2 Chr. 29:1), whom he succeeded on the throne of the kingdom of Judah. He reigned twenty-nine years (B.C. 726-697).

people.name: Ahaz
people.summary: The son and successor of Jotham, king of Judah (2 Kings 16; Isa. 7-9; 2 Chr. 28). He gave himself up to a life of wickedness and idolatry. Notwithstanding the remonstrances and warnings of Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah, he appealed for help against Rezin, king of Damascus, and Pekah, king of Israel, who threatened Jerusalem, to Tiglath-pileser, the king of Assyria, to the great injury of his kingdom and his own humilating subjection to the Assyrians (2 Kings 16:7, 9; 15:29).

people.name: Hoshea
people.summary: The last king of Israel. He conspired against and slew his predecessor, Pekah (Isa. 7:16), but did not ascend the throne till after an interregnum of warfare of eight years (2 Kings 17:1, 2).

people.name: Elah
people.summary: The father of Hoshea, the last king of Israel (2 Kings 15:30; 17:1).

people.name: Abijah
people.summary: The daughter of Zechariah (2 Chr. 29:1; comp. Isa. 8:2), and afterwards the wife of Ahaz.

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: The father of Abijah, who was the mother of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:1).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Shalmaneser
people.summary: An Assyrian king (Hos. 10:14), identified with Shalmaneser II. (Sayce) or IV. (Lenormant), the successor of Pul on the throne of Assyria (B.C. 728).

people.name: Sennacherib
people.summary: Sin (the god) sends many brothers, son of Sargon, whom he succeeded on the throne of Assyria (B.C. 705), in the 23rd year of Hezekiah. “Like the Persian Xerxes, he was weak and vainglorious, cowardly under reverse, and cruel and boastful in success.”

people.name: Rabshakeh
people.summary: Chief of the princes, the name given to the chief cup-bearer or the vizier of the Assyrian court; one of Sennacherib’s messengers to Hezekiah.

people.name: Tartan
people.summary: One of Sennacherib’s messengers to Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:17).

people.name: Rabsaris
people.summary: Chief of the Heads, one of the three officers whom Sennacherib sent from Lachish with a threatening message to Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17; Jer. 39:3, 13).

people.name: Eliakim
people.summary: The son of Hilkiah, who was sent to receive the message of the invading Assyrians and report it to Isaiah (2 Kings 18:18; 19:2; Isa. 36:3; 37:2).

people.name: Shebna
people.summary: Tender youth, “treasurer” over the house in the reign of Hezekiah, i.e., comptroller or governor of the palace. On account of his pride he was ejected from his office, and Eliakim was promoted to it (Isa. 22:15-25).

people.name: Joah
people.summary: The son of Asaph, and “recorder” or chronicler to King Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18, 26, 37).

people.name: Hilkiah
people.summary: The father of Eliakim (2 Kings 18:18, 26, 37).

people.name: Asaph
people.summary: The “recorder” in the time of Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18, 37).

people.name: Pharaoh
people.summary: Pharaoh, in whom Hezekiah put his trust in his war against Sennacherib (2 Kings 18:21).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Assyria
places.summary: The name derived from the city Asshur on the Tigris, the original capital of the country, was originally a colony from Babylonia, and was ruled by viceroys from that kingdom.

places.name: Gaza
places.summary: Called also Azzah, which is its Hebrew name (Deut. 2:23; 1 Kings 4:24; Jer. 25:20), strong, a city on the Mediterranean shore, remarkable for its early importance as the chief centre of a great commercial traffic with Egypt.

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Gozan
places.summary: A region in Central Asia to which the Israelites were carried away captive (2 Kings 17:6; 1 Chr. 5:26; 2 Kings 19:12; Isa. 37:12). It was situated in Mesopotamia, on the river Habor (2 Kings 17:6; 18:11), the Khabur, a tributary of the Euphrates.

places.name: Habor
places.summary: The united stream, or, according to others, with beautiful banks, the name of a river in Assyria, and also of the district through which it flowed (1 Chr. 5:26).

places.name: Halah
places.summary: A district of Media to which captive Israelites were transported by the Assyrian kings (2 Kings 17:6; 18:11; 1 Chr. 5:26). It lay along the banks of the upper Khabur, from its source to its junction with the Jerujer.

places.name: Judah (Southern)
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1257 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Lachish
places.summary: Impregnable, a royal Canaanitish city in the Shephelah, or maritime plain of Palestine (Josh. 10:3, 5; 12:11). It was taken and destroyed by the Israelites (Josh. 10:31-33).

places.name: Field
places.summary: A spot near Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17; Isa. 36:2; 7:3), on the side of the highway west of the city, not far distant from the “upper pool” at the head of the valley of Hinnom.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Arpad
places.summary: (Isa. 10:9; 36:19; 37:13), also Arphad, support, a Syrian city near Hamath, along with which it is invariably mentioned (2 Kings 19:13; 18:34; Isa. 10:9), and Damascus (Jer. 49:23).

places.name: Hamath
places.summary: Fortress, the capital of one of the kingdoms of Upper Syria of the same name, on the Orontes, in the valley of Lebanon, at the northern boundary of Palestine (Num. 13:21; 34:8), at the foot of Hermon (Josh. 13:5) towards Damascus (Zech. 9:2; Jer. 49:23).

places.name: Hena
places.summary: One of the cities of Mesopotamia destroyed by sennacherib (2 Kings 18:34; 19:13).

places.name: Ivvah
places.summary: Overturning, a city of the Assyrians, whence colonists were brought to Samaria (2 Kings 18:34; 19:13).

places.name: Sepharvaim
places.summary: Taken by Sargon, king of Assyria (2 Kings 17:24; 18:34; 19:13; Isa. 37:13). It was a double city, and received the common name Sepharvaim, i.e., “the two Sipparas,” or “the two booktowns.”

events.title: Reign of Hezekiah
events.summary: Passage: 2 Kings 18:1–20:21. People: Hezekiah. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 29 years.
